title: Why Does Toast Land Butter-Side Down? #science #physics
description:
It's not bad luck and it's not the butter: it's mostly the height of your table. Toast sliding off the edge pivots on the rim and starts to spin. From a 75 cm table the fall takes about 0.4 seconds, only enough for about half a turn, so butter-up becomes butter-down. From a table about 3 m high it would turn roughly a full turn and land butter up.

Caveat: a fast sideways flick changes the outcome; this is for toast that slides or is nudged off.

More on spinning things on camera: Why do wheels spin backwards on camera? https://youtu.be/SxjS9sdc_Ek

Sources
- Matthews, R. A. J. (1995), Tumbling toast, Murphy's Law and the fundamental constants, European Journal of Physics 16: 172–176
- Bacon, M. E., Heald, G. & James, M. (2001), A closer look at tumbling toast, American Journal of Physics 69: 38–43
- Fall time computed: t = √(2h/g) = 0.39 s for h = 0.75 m

Try it with a slice of bread (no butter) from a higher shelf: does it land differently?

Script, voice and animation are AI-produced (Claude; Kokoro voice). Every claim is checked against the sources above.
